0.note: The word translated as **chief musician** likely refers to the person in charge of music for worship. Some languages may have a term for a music leader. Alternate translation: [For the music director] or [For the leader of worship music]
Here **palm** and **hand** represent power or control. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the control of all his enemies]

1.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strength**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the one who makes me strong]

2.note: David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were actually a high **rock** that he could climb up to reach safety from danger. If it would be helpful in your language, you could express this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [Yahweh is like a rock that keeps me safe from danger … he is like a rock to me]

Here David is speaking as if Yahweh were actually a **stronghold** or a strong structure where people go to be protected. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and my place of safety]

Here David uses **take refuge in him** as if God were a place of safety in which he could hide. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I depend on him to keep me safe] or [I trust him to protect me]

Here David is speaking of Yahweh as if he were a **shield** that protected him from attack. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [my protector]

David is using the possessive form to describe a **horn** that is characterized by providing **salvation**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and the horn that saves me]

David is speaking of God’s power to save him as if it were a powerful **horn** of an animal. A horn was a symbol of strength in ancient Israelite culture because animals use their horns as weapons. Your language may have a comparable expression that you could use, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the one who saves me by his power] or [and the one who powerfully saves me]

3.note: The expression **being praised** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I call to Yahweh, the one whom people praise] or [I call to Yahweh, the one whom I praise]

The expression **I am saved** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [and he saves me]

4.note: Here David is speaking as if death were actually **cords** that could wrap around and bind a person. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If not, you could state this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [Death threatened to bind me like cords] or [I was in danger of dying]

David speaks here of **torrents of wickedness** as if wickedness were a flood of rushing water that could overwhelm and destroy him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [a wicked person was pursuing me relentlessly, and that terrified me]

5.note: Here, **Sheol**, the dwelling place of the dead according to Hebrew culture, represents death itself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [The cords of death surrounded me]

David is speaking as if Sheol or death actually had **cords** that it could use to bind him. This suggests he felt trapped in a situation where he thought he would die. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. You could also use plain language. Alternate translation: [I thought I was bound to die]

David speaks here of **snares of death** as if death were a hunter that could set traps for people. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. You could also use plain language. Alternate translation: [death had me in its clutches]

6.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **distress**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [When I was distressed] or [When I felt distressed]

Here, **to his face** represents being in God’s presence or coming before him. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and my call for help]

Here, **voice** represents the words David spoke in his prayer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [He heard my prayer]

By **his temple**, David means God’s temple in heaven. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from his heavenly temple]
David is using the term **ears** to mean hearing. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he heard]

7.q: וַ⁠תִּגְעַ֬שׁ וַ⁠תִּרְעַ֨שׁ ׀ הָ⁠אָ֗רֶץ וּ⁠מוֹסְדֵ֣י הָרִ֣ים יִרְגָּ֑זוּ וַ֝⁠יִּתְגָּֽעֲשׁ֗וּ כִּי־חָ֥רָה לֽ⁠וֹ
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Then, because it burned to him, the earth shook and trembled. The foundations of the heavens quaked and shook themselves]

The terms that the ULT translates as **shook** and **shook themselves** represent two different verbs in the original. Hebrew had more synonyms for this idea than some other languages may have. David expresses some of these with the verbs translated as **trembled** and **quaked**. It may be necessary for you to use the same words rather than different ones. However, if you do have a variety of terms for this, it would be appropriate to use different words for **shook** and **shook themselves**.

The terms **shook** and **trembled** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [Then the earth shook violently]

7.q: וַ⁠תִּגְעַ֬שׁ וַ⁠תִּרְעַ֨שׁ ׀ הָ⁠אָ֗רֶץ וּ⁠מוֹסְדֵ֣י הָרִ֣ים יִרְגָּ֑זוּ וַ֝⁠יִּתְגָּֽעֲשׁ֗וּ
7.note: David is speaking as if the **earth** and the **foundations of the mountains** were actually a person who could shake and tremble. This expresses how powerfully God responded to David’s prayer. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Then it was as though a violent earthquake occurred and shook the earth and the foundations of the mountains]

The terms **quaked** and **shook themselves** mean similar things. David is using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [quaked mightily]
Here, **it burned to him** represents his anger. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he was angry]

8.q: עָ֘לָ֤ה עָשָׁ֨ן ׀ בְּ⁠אַפּ֗⁠וֹ וְ⁠אֵשׁ־מִ⁠פִּ֥י⁠ו תֹּאכֵ֑ל גֶּ֝חָלִ֗ים בָּעֲר֥וּ מִמֶּֽ⁠נּוּ
8.note: David is saying that when Yahweh came to help him, Yahweh’s power was so great that it was like a volcano. David describes the opening at the top of a volcano, from which **Smoke** and **fire** and **Coals** come out, as if it were the **nose** and **mouth** of the volcano. If your readers would be familiar with what a volcano is, you could express in your translation how David is using a volcano as an image to describe Yahweh’s power. If not, you could describe in more general terms how Yahweh’s power is like fire and smoke.

David is speaking of the fire that comes from a volcano, which represents God here, as if it were a wild animal that **devoured** its prey. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and fire from his mouth completely destroyed everything] or [and fire from his mouth consumed everything]

9.q: וַ⁠יֵּ֣ט שָׁ֭מַיִם וַ⁠יֵּרַ֑ד וַ֝⁠עֲרָפֶ֗ל תַּ֣חַת רַגְלָֽי⁠ו
9.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And he came standing on a dark cloud, and thus he lowered the heavens]

10.note: The words **rode** and **flew** express a single idea. The word **flew** tells more about how he **rode**. If it would be more natural in your language, you could express this meaning in a different way. Alternate translation: [And he flew by riding on a cherub]

David is speaking as if God were actually riding on a **cherub** and flying through the sky. This is part of a poetic description of God’s power and swift action to help David. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he came very quickly]

David is speaking as if the wind actually had **wings** and that it could fly through the sky carrying Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it appeared as if the wind were a great bird that was carrying him swiftly]

11.note: David is speaking as if the darkness were actually **set** like a physical object that could be arranged in place. He means that God caused darkness to surround himself. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [It was as if he were dwelling within the darkness of the storm]

11.q: יָ֤שֶׁת חֹ֨שֶׁךְ ׀ סִתְר֗⁠וֹ סְבִֽיבוֹתָ֥י⁠ו סֻכָּת֑⁠וֹ חֶשְׁכַת־מַ֝֗יִם
11.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [He set darkness as his covering—yes, the shelter around him was dark storm clouds]

12.note: Here, **before him** represents being in God’s presence. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in his presence]

David assumes that readers will know that **coals of fire** means “flashes of lightning.” You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and flashes of lightning] of [and bolts of lightning]

13.note: Some ancient manuscripts include the words **hailstones and coals of fire**. The ULT follows that reading. Other ancient manuscripts do not have these words. It is possible that during the process of copying, they were repeated here from the previous verse. The ancient Greek translation does not have them. If a translation of the Bible exists in your region, you may wish to use the reading that it uses. If a translation of the Bible does not exist in your region, you may wish to use the reading of the ULT.

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [there were hailstones and coals of fire]

14.q: וַ⁠יִּשְׁלַ֣ח חִ֭צָּי⁠ו וַ⁠יְפִיצֵ֑⁠ם וּ⁠בְרָקִ֥ים רָ֝ב וַ⁠יְהֻמֵּֽ⁠ם
14.note: Here David is using an image within an image. Within the image of a thunderstorm that represents Yahweh coming powerfully to help him, David speaks of lightning bolts as if they were **arrows**. You might be able to clarify this by combining the two parts of this verse, which mean basically the same thing. Alternate translation: [And he sent out lightning bolts like arrows and panicked them so that they scattered]

The pronoun **them** refers in each instance to David’s enemies. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and he scattered my enemies … and he panicked those enemies]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [yes, and he sent out lightnings in abundance]

15.q: וַ⁠יֵּ֤רָא֨וּ ׀ אֲפִ֥יקֵי מַ֗יִם וַֽ⁠יִּגָּלוּ֮ מוֹסְד֪וֹת תֵּ֫בֵ֥ל
15.note: The expressions **were seen** and **were uncovered** are passive verbal forms. If your language would not use those forms, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And the channels of the sea became visible; ground no longer covered the foundations of the world]

15.q: וַ⁠יֵּ֤רָא֨וּ ׀ אֲפִ֥יקֵי מַ֗יִם וַֽ⁠יִּגָּלוּ֮ מוֹסְד֪וֹת תֵּ֫בֵ֥ל מִ⁠גַּעֲרָ֣תְ⁠ךָ֣ יְהוָ֑ה מִ֝⁠נִּשְׁמַ֗ת ר֣וּחַ אַפֶּֽ⁠ךָ
15.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [And at the rebuke of Yahweh, from the blast of the breath of his nose, the channels of the sea were seen, the foundations of the world were uncovered]

16.note: David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [He stretched out his hand]
Here, **height** represents “heaven” as God’s dwelling place. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [from heaven]
Here, **many waters** represents the sea. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [out of the sea]

Here, **many waters**, meaning the sea, represents deep trouble or dangerous situations. David uses this image because he had earlier described his enemies as dangerous flood waters. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [out of great trouble]

17.q: יַצִּילֵ֗⁠נִי מֵ⁠אֹיְבִ֥⁠י עָ֑ז וּ֝⁠מִ⁠שֹּׂנְאַ֗⁠י כִּֽי־אָמְצ֥וּ מִמֶּֽ⁠נִּי
17.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [Because they were stronger than me, he delivered me from my strong enemy, from the ones hating me]

18.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **calamity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [on a day that would have been disastrous for me]

19.note: Here David is speaking of being rescued as if he had been squeezed into a narrow space and God brought him out to an **open space**. The image suggests that David had been in a dangerous situation with no way to escape, but God enabled him to escape. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And he set me free from danger] or [And he rescued me from my desperate situation]

If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase **delivered me** describes. Alternate translation: [because he delighted in me, he delivered me]

20.q: יִגְמְלֵ֣⁠נִי יְהוָ֣ה כְּ⁠צִדְקִ֑⁠י כְּ⁠בֹ֥ר יָ֝דַ֗⁠י יָשִׁ֥יב לִֽ⁠י
20.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. The second emphasizes the meaning of the first by repeating the same idea with different words. Hebrew poetry was based on this kind of repetition, and you may want to show this to your readers by including both phrases in your translation. If it is helpful, you could connect the phrases in a way that shows that the second phrase is repeating the first one, not saying something additional. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has rewarded me according to my righteousness; yes, according to the cleanness of my hands he has given back to me]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **righteousness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [according to the right things I have done] or [because I have acted righteously]

David is speaking of his actions as if they were his **hands**, which could be physically clean or dirty. He means that his behavior has been morally pure. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly here and in verse 25. Alternate translation: [according to the innocence of my actions]

David is using **he has given back to me** as a common expression of his culture to mean “he has treated me in the same way.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he has treated me in the same way]

21.note: Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation. If the connection between this statement and the previous one is not clear, you may want to use a different connecting word to show how this statement relates to what comes before it. Alternate translation: [After all,]

David is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a way or path that the person was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I have lived as Yahweh commands] or [I have obeyed Yahweh’s commands]

David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context, specifically in the next verse, if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [and I have not been so wicked as to turn away from my God]

22.note: Here the word **For** introduces not a reason but an explanation of why Yahweh has rewarded David according to his righteousness. If it would be clearer in your language, you could use a word that introduces an explanation. Alternate translation: [Indeed,]

David is speaking of **judgments** as if they were objects that could be physically placed in front of him. This means that he constantly remembers and thinks about God’s laws. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I am always mindful of his judgments]

David is speaking of God’s **statutes** as if they were objects that he could physically turn away from. Your language may have a comparable expression you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and I have not disobeyed his statutes]

23.note: David is using the possessive form to mean sin that he could have committed. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [from any iniquity that I might have committed]

24.note: See how you translated the phrase **according to my righteousness** in 18:20.
See how you translated the phrase **according to the cleanness of my hands** in 18:20.

Here, **before his eyes** represents how God sees and evaluates people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in his judgment] or [by his standards]

25.note: David is using the adjective **faithful** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [To people who are faithful]

26.note: The expression **the purified** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [those who purify themselves] or [those who keep themselves pure]

Here David is speaking of people who deliberately do what is wrong as if they were physically **crooked** or bent. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [those who do evil] or [those who are dishonest]

27.note: Here David is speaking as if oppressed or poor people were **lowly**, that is, in a physically low place, and as if proud people were physically **high**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [an oppressed people … prideful people] or [poor people … prideful people]

Here, **eyes** represents the proud looks or arrogant attitude of people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but the proud looks of the ones being high, you humble]

28.q: אַ֭תָּה תָּאִ֣יר נֵרִ֑⁠י יְהוָ֥ה אֱ֝לֹהַ֗⁠י יַגִּ֥יהַּ חָשְׁכִּֽ⁠י
28.note: Here David is speaking as if his life were actually **a lamp** that God lights and as if his troubles were actually **darkness** that God brightens. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. If not, you could state this as a comparison. Alternate translation: [you give me life like lighting a lamp; Yahweh my God helps me through troubles like someone who brightens darkness]

29.note: This could mean: (1) that David is saying that by God’s help, he can pursue and overtake a **troop**. He may be recalling how he and his men were able to overtake the Amalekite “troop” (1 Samuel 30:8) that had raided Ziklag and rescue their families and possessions. Alternate translation: [I can pursue and overtake a raiding band], or (2) that David is saying that by God’s help, he can directly attack and disperse an opposing group of soldiers. Alternate translation: [I can run through a troop] or [I can attack and disperse an opposing troop]

David is speaking of successfully leading troops to capture a fortified city as if he and they would **leap** over its walls. He may be recalling how he and his soldiers were able to capture the stronghold of Zion in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:6–9). If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [I can surmount the walls of a fortified city]

30.note: Here David is speaking of how God acts and directs others as if it were a **way** or path that he was walking along. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [everything he does is faultless] or [he always acts righteously]
Here, **word of Yahweh** represents what Yahweh says by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [What Yahweh says]

The expression **is refined** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you need to say who does the action, the context indicates that it is God. Alternate translation: [is pure]

David is speaking as if God were actually **a shield** behind which people take **refuge**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [He protects everyone who trusts him]

31.q: כִּ֤י מִ֣י אֱ֭לוֹהַּ מִ⁠בַּלְעֲדֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וּ⁠מִ֥י צ֝֗וּר זוּלָתִ֥⁠י אֱלֹהֵֽי⁠נוּ
31.note: David is using the question form for emphasis. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate these questions as statements or as exclamations. Alternate translation: [For Yahweh is the only God! And our God is the only rock!]

David speaks of God here as if he were a **rock** that people can hide behind or stand on for safety. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use a comparable expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [provides safety]

32.note: Here David is speaking of valor as if it were a piece of clothing with which God **is the one girding** him, like a belt or piece of armor. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [makes me valiant]

This could mean: (1) that God makes the **way** on which a person travels **perfect**, that is, free from obstacles. Alternate translation: [and he removes all the obstacles in my path] or [and he enables me to live the life he has chosen for me without hindrance], or (2) that David is speaking of how a person lives as if that were a **way** or path that the person is walking along. Alternate translation: [and he enables me to live in just the way that he wants people to live]

33.note: David is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [making my feet like the feet of a deer]

Here David is comparing his ability to move quickly and surely with the way a deer moves in difficult terrain. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [making my feet secure] or [keeping me from stumbling]

David may be using this possessive form, referring to these as **my high places**, because he is recalling how he had to hide among cliffs when Saul was trying to kill him. It may be more natural in your language to express this meaning with a different form. Alternate translation: [and he keeps me from falling from any high places where I have to go]

34.note: David is using his **hands** to represent all of him in the act of fighting in battle. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [training me for war]

35.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **salvation**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And the shield you provide for me saves me]

Here David is speaking of God’s power to save him as if it were a **shield** that could protect him from physical attacks. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you protect me by saving me]

Here, **right hand** represents the power of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and your power]

By **your humility**, David means God’s humbleness in responding to his prayers requesting help. Because God was much greater and more powerful than David, David views God’s response to his prayers as an act of humility. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and your answer to my prayers] or [and your humble answer to my prayers]

36.note: Here David’s **step** represents the place where he would step. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [You enlarge the place where I step under me]

David is speaking as if God had made the area where he needed to walk more spacious. This represents having freedom to move and act without being constrained by enemies. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. You could also use plain language. Alternate translation: [You give me room to maneuver]

38.note: David is describing one event before describing another event that preceded it. If it would be helpful your language, you may wish to relate these events in the order in which they happened, as in the UST. Alternate translation: [so that they fall under my feet and were not able to arise]
The implication is that David’s enemies fall and remain dead. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [they fall down dead]

39.note: Here David is speaking as if God were actually girding him **with valor**, as if valor were a belt or sash that could be wrapped around him. David means that God gives him courage and strength for battle. See how you translated a similar expression in 18:32. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [And you make me valiant]

David means that people who try to rebel against him ultimately **bow down** as a symbolic action by which they show renewed submission to his authority. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [you make the ones rising up under me submit humbly to my authority]
